Every nonzero number raised to the power.why: A school rule stated in many forms ('x^0 = 1', 'to the power of 0 is 1', 'to the zero power is 1'); Wikipedia gives it as the definition of a zero exponent.

sources.quote: A number raised to the 0 power is generally defined to be 1

sources.query: to the power of zero is one
to the power of zero is 1
any number to the power of 0 is 1

notes: TBox rule, stored (very_unlikely). 'Nonzero' keeps it free of exceptions (R1: 0⁰ is undefined or 1 by convention). The counterfactual (x⁰ = 0) is a common beginner's error, so it is plausible and clearly false. Mathematics TBox: every derived query is determinate. A well-known member (an equilateral triangle, 7, 2) belongs to its class by definition, so the world where it leaves the class and keeps its stored value contradicts arithmetic or geometry, and the world where it keeps both its membership and its stored value contradicts the edit: no world is left but the one the rule forces. Its stored value is what a patch-only model gives. New members named in the prompt: q and z = 3.71. Well-known members: 10⁰ (stored from scientific notation) and 2⁰. Locality: the near query (multiplying by 1) shares the topic; queries about x¹ or x/x were avoided, because the exponent laws tie them to x⁰ (x¹ = x¹ · x⁰) and they would not be unrelated. Relation: power_zero_equals (functional: a number raised to the power 0 has one value), not the general 'equals', since the rule gives every nonzero number one value of x⁰. The well-known members' stored values (10⁰ = 1, 2⁰ = 1) give way, as their chains state.
